raw_profile.bio:
Emma is a Lecturer in Education and Gender at IOE, UCL's Faculty of Education and Society.

 

Emma's research is informed by feminist epistemologies and decoloniality. She is particularly interested in how knowledges about gender and sexuality come into being (and/or are excluded) in education and global policy. She has conducted research on this theme at the United Nations Commission on the Status of Women (CSW) and in higher education settings. Emma's research typically draws on qualitative and post-qualitative approaches and explores the inseparability of ethics, ontology and epistemology in research methodologies.

Emma has research consultancy experience and has led research projects for

- The Overseas Development Institute (ODI) on their Gender Adolescence: Global Evidence (GAGE) project
- The Global Interagency Security Forum (GISF) on a research project about the Security Risk Management of Aid Workers with Diverse Profiles

 

She is available for consultancy work on issues related to gender, sexuality and higher education. 

 

Emma's PhD was funded by an Excellence Scholarship from the University of East London. She holds a MA in Education, Gender and International Development and a MRes in Education and Social Research Methods from the UCL Institute of Education. Her academic and professional background includes a BSc in Geology and Geography and a PGCE in Geography from the University of Birmingham. She has taught Geography, Sex and Relationships Education, and History at secondary schools in the UK, China and Thailand.

raw_profile.research_interests:
Emma is currently Co-I on the following research projects:

1. A UCL funded research project titled: The experiences of LGBTQ+ staff at UCL (with Dr Simon Lock in STS) (2021 - Current)

2. A CPA seed funded project titled: Discomfort in Qualitative Inquiry (with Dr Mark Hardman (UCL), Prof Carol Taylor (University of Bath), Dr Joy Cranham (University of Bath), Mir Abdullah Miri (University of Bath), Nai Lang (University of Bath), Hannah Hogarth (University of Northampton) (2025 - 2026)


Recent Research Funding:

Grand Challenges Project Funding (2024): Decolonising PhD supervision and Research (with Dr Leda Kamenpoulou in PHD and Dr Laila Kadiwal in EPS). The Research Assistant on this project is Sadaf Yasir (PhD Candidate in EPS). The aim of this project is to develop a toolkit for PhD supervisors.


Project outputs include:
. An annotated bibliography of research articles and grey literature
. A workshop for UCL staff on Decolonising PhD Supervision and Research - Held on 18th July 2024

IOE International Engagement Funding (2024). This funding was used to host a 'festival of events' inspired by the GFRN & qUCL joint annual lecture by Dr Rahul Rao on the 'Libidinal Lives of Statues'.

 

Project outputs include:
. a video recording of Rahul Rao's annual lecture and panel responses from Sophie Chauhan, Subhadra Das and Dr Shikha Dilawri
. Think Pieces podcast with Dr Rahul Rao hosted by Dr Sean Curran
. Think Pieces publication by Sophie Chauhan (PhD candidate in Race, Ethnicity and Postcolonial Studies at UCL)
. 'The Belle Statue' Panel Discussion & Workshop Event (forthcoming) hosted by Carmela Morgillo (PhD Candidate, UCL School of Slavonic and East European Studies)

 

Centre for Teachers and Teaching Research (2021). This research project using walking interviews to understand PGCE student experiences of racialisation while training to become teachers (with Dr Mark Hardman and Alison Wiggins in CPA and Dr Lauren Hammond at Oxford University)
